newsitem.title: UK: UK to standardise rules for "listed" TV sports.
newsitem.headline: UK to standardise rules for "listed" TV sports.

text.p: The British government said on Thursday it was taking soundings on the criteria to use in deciding which sports events should be set aside for live broadcast on free-to-air television channels.
Broadcasters, sports bodies and viewers' groups will all be consulted as part of the government's review of the list of events for which live TV coverage must be offered to the "free" channels.

The government hopes to complete the consultation by the end of the month. Suggestions for changes to the eight-event list will be sought once criteria have been established, National Heritage Minister Mark Fisher said.
The list includes the Olympic Games, soccer's World Cup finals, England test cricket and the finals weekend of the Wimbledon tennis championship.
Pay-television operator BSkyB Plc has bought up the rights to many top sports events, using them to win over subscribers to its services.
BSkyB maintains that it has multiplied the amount of sport shown on television and increased the value of sports rights.
But BSkyB's critics argue that its tactics deprive the 75 percent of the population without pay television of access to key sporting fixtures.
Fisher said finding a balance was crucial.

"The new Government firmly believes that events which play a significant part in our culture should be seen on national television by everyone who wants to watch them. That is why we support the principle of listing events," he said in a written parliamentary answer.

"(But) we do not want to deprive the holders of broadcast sports rights of income which is used for the benefit of players and fans, or to deny the important role subscription broadcasters have played in bringing more sports coverage than ever before to our television screens," he added.
